1601734662325686273.a: Why are there so many similar stories around the world of the ancient past? It seems to me like the answer is that we, absolutely know that we, all came from the same place going back far enough. Some pockets of people spread around the world with similar stories.

1601734664187961344.a: You can see the ghost of Hermes/Osiris/Sokar/Whoever wandering around the world pretty clearly if you know what you are looking at. Does that mean a single DNA group wandered? Nope, people traded stories and ways of teaching and those project ghosts on the walls of our reality.

1601734666200883200.a: There definitely have been people who made it their mission ensure that core knowledge (Language, Math, Farming, Medicine, Manufacturing, etc) was distributed around the world. This I know. I don't believe. They are bound by an evolving set of knowledge instead of genetics.

1601734668088672256.a: When did hominids start doing this? Archaeologists find advanced knowledge at 13,000+ year old sites like Tas Tepeler. We find evidence of advanced knowledge all over the world. Devolving, being lost, and found again. We see it evolve over time at the sites around Tas Tepeler.

1601734669938016257.a: Does that mean there was some vast interlinked civilization? No, of course not. It means people wrote things down, had time to rediscover the parts they lost. Its's taken us only 400 years to go from iron age to alien mothership. There's no way to know if it happened before.

1601734671913562112.a: You could search every site on Earth and never find it. Maybe right under your nose. I think we need more cross discipline scientists. I think this debate between Graham and Old PhDs will show that we just need a new perspective; one our young scientists seem to be evolving today

1601736535295918080.a: When people say "but we don't find" I will point out humans almost always live near major bodies of water.
